items.description: During a standard survey, scientists made a surprising discovery—a rare yellow burbot in Lake Ontario. items.description: Public sector workers in Canada's Nova Scotia province could receive up to C$5,000 each under a C$470 million compensation deal approved by a court. The settlement follows a ruling that declared a 2015 law restricting wage increases and long-service benefits unconstitutional. Around 81,000 workers may qualify for wage-related damages, while payments must be completed by December 31, 2027.

items.author: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK
items.description: In a landmark ruling, a New South Wales court has declared a $6.2 million home sale in Bronte void, citing undisclosed development plans. Buyers discovered a looming nine-storey structure that would block their ocean views just after signing the contract. The ruling emphasized that agents misrepresented crucial information. Following the legal wrangling, the property eventually sold for just $5.1 million, underscoring the critical need for transparency in real estate dealings.

items.title: Boy's promise to repay neighbour's kindness feeds 29,000 families at Thanksgiving
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: Rob Adams fulfilled a childhood vow to assist needy families by establishing Thanksgiving Heroes. This initiative has grown nationwide, impacting over 29,000 families since it started. The organization prioritizes delivering meals to families selected by their communities, eliminating the need for proof of need. Local affiliates operate independently while maintaining the mission of families assisting families. There are plans to expand meal distributions to 3,600 families by 2026.

items.title: Why does your Wi-Fi work even when radio signals bounce off walls?
items.author: TRENDING DESK
items.description: The evolution of Wi-Fi technology is a fascinating tale of global collaboration. It began with Hedy Lamarr and George Antheil's innovative frequency-hopping idea during World War II. Subsequent advancements were made by CSIRO researchers in Australia, who enhanced indoor wireless communication. The U.S. played a crucial role by opening up radio frequencies for unlicensed use, setting standards that paved the way for the wireless networks we rely on today.

items.description: A Delhi court has upheld an order directing a man and his wife to vacate a room in his 65-year-old widowed mother's house, where she let them stay temporarily out of love and affection. District judge Sumit Dalal held they are licensees with no legal right, rejected their adverse possession plea and gave them 30 days to vacate.

items.title: 22 years after gifting property, K'taka woman fails to reclaim it from daughter-in-law
items.author: TOI CITY DESK
items.description: The Karnataka High Court recently overturned a tribunal's decision to cancel a 2000 property gift deed. The elderly woman claimed that her daughter-in-law obtained the deed through fraud, but the court found otherwise. The gift deed was registered and the transfer was legally completed prior to the relevant law's enactment. The sister-in-law will continue payments of Rs 4,000 each month to her mother-in-law as directed by the court.

items.title: Father-in-law must provide shelter before evicting widowed daughter-in-law: HC
items.author: TOI CITY DESK
items.description: The Delhi High Court recently ruled in favor of a widowed woman regarding her residence rights. While recognizing her father-in-law's ownership, the court emphasized the woman's need for housing support. The court's order allows her to remain until he secures alternative accommodation or pays monthly rent. Additionally, the ruling reaffirms her entitlement under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act.

items.title: Indiana stepdad's adoption overturned after mother blocks birth dad's contact
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: An Indiana stepfather’s adoption of his wife’s daughter has been reversed by an appeals court. The ruling found that the biological father's limited contact was largely a result of the mother's attempts to limit his access. Evidence indicated he sought involvement and provided financial support. The majority opinion pointed out discrepancies in the mother’s testimony compared to previous court decisions, leading to a remand for further custody deliberations.

items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: Montana's Supreme Court has mandated that a lower court revisit the distribution of a deceased man's estate to his widow. After Sara's passing, her son continued her pursuit, focusing on the property's valuation.

items.title: Nick Jonas urges parents to keep phones in another room to be present for kids
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: During an enlightening discussion with Lewis Howes, Nick Jonas disclosed his insights on parenting. He shared how having a daughter has significantly enriched his experience, supported by his partner, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, as they embark on this journey of parenthood together.

items.author: ALIM SHAIKH
items.description: NCP (SP) MLA Jitendra Awhad confirmed the party's support for the delimitation bill after meeting Sharad Pawar. Baramati MP Supriya Sule stated that the party would examine the draft before making a decision. She will miss the INDIA bloc meeting due to her father's hospitalization, delegating the representation to Amol Kolhe. The Union cabinet has approved the proposed legislation, set for discussion during a special Lok Sabha session.

items.title: Alexandria dig uncovers possible royal tomb tunnel, but identity remain unknown
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: Archaeologists have unveiled an impressive limestone foundation in Alexandria that may belong to a royal tomb. The site, located in the ancient Royal Quarter, features a mysterious tunnel and a distinctive square structure. Experts believe this could be linked to Ptolemy IV Philopator and potentially serve a funerary purpose. A dedicated committee is examining the architectural details, while further excavations promise to illuminate Alexandria's fascinating historical narrative.

items.title: US pushed Venezuela, Iraq to quit OPEC to boost oil output: Report
items.author: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA
items.description: The United States influenced both Venezuela and Iraq regarding their membership in OPEC earlier this year. After the removal of Nicolás Maduro, discussions were opened about Venezuela potentially leaving the organization. Prime Minister Ali Faleh al-Zaidi also contemplated Iraq's OPEC exit amid US investment talks. Ultimately, Iraq's oil ministry convinced him to stay and seek a higher production quota.

items.title: How BJP, DMK's year-long negotiations paved way for delimitation deal
items.author: JULIE MARIAPPAN
items.description: After intense negotiations, DMK decides to support the BJP-led Union government's delimitation bill, a notable change from their previous stance. This strategic move comes after discussions concerning proportional seat adjustments and census freezes. DMK aims to balance its political aspirations while safeguarding Tamil Nadu's representation in the Lok Sabha, underscoring that party interests remain a top priority amid earlier fears of losing seats.

items.title: 'Siraj needs help': Ashwin urges India team to show compassion after repeated snubs
items.author: PRANAV SHUKLA
items.description: R Ashwin emphasized the importance of supporting Mohammed Siraj during his recent team exclusions. Ashwin suggested that a sports psychologist could help Siraj navigate his feelings during this challenging time. Siraj has remained professional and supportive of his teammates despite feeling disappointed about being left out.

items.author: SAURABH SINHA
items.description: Adani Group has expressed its intention to invest in the airline industry to support growth and expansion. The group's CFO mentioned that India's aviation market has significant untapped potential, with approximately 60 crore potential passengers. Current government regulations limit the group's equity stake in scheduled airlines, prompting a request for an exemption. They aim to enhance passenger services and address existing route limitations across the country.

items.description: The Sir Dorabji Tata Trust has filed caveats following complaints from vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh regarding a lawsuit. This comes on the heels of previous apprehensions voiced by the vice-chairmen on trustee appointments and matters involving Tata Sons, which previously hindered board agreements and the annual general meeting.

items.title: Minority shareholders’ interest protection a key priority: Sebi
items.author: TNN
items.description: Sebi chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey highlighted the priority of protecting minority shareholders amid concerns regarding the Tata Steel-APL Apollo transaction. The structure and valuation of the deal have raised questions from proxy advisory firms, necessitating further review. Tata Steel plans to acquire a significant stake in APL Apollo Tubes while simultaneously selling its steel businesses. Sebi is also focusing on improving compliance processes for stock brokers and reviewing IPO regulations.

items.title: Support to Bill may not automatically lead DMK to NDA, but will open alignment path
items.author: KUMAR RAKESH
items.description: In an unexpected twist, the DMK is contemplating supporting the BJP on the delimitation bill after years of opposition. The BJP has offered several concessions to entice DMK's cooperation. This potential alliance highlights the complex and often shifting landscape of Indian politics, especially with the rise of Vijay's TVK, which narrows DMK's choices. Thus, political survival may compel them to forge an unlikely bond with the BJP.

items.title: Congress says BJP wants to change Constitution, compromised CEC will redraw LS seats
items.author: TNN
items.description: The opposition faces a critical challenge with the proposed delimitation bill, as the DMK and NCP show support for it. Congress has raised alarms, accusing the BJP of trying to circumvent constitutional norms. After disappointing electoral results, there are fears of manipulated outcomes. Amid shifting alliances, Congress grapples with decisions that have upset DMK leadership, making the future of unity within the opposition uncertain.

items.title: 'Unacceptable': EAM Jaishankar condemns attack on seafarers, maritime shipping
items.author: TNN
items.description: EAM S Jaishankar addressed the IORA, advocating for a unified global response to maritime attacks and ensuring safety. The joint communique emphasized respect for international law and commitments to maritime peace and stability. PM Narendra Modi engaged with foreign ministers from 23 member-states during the meeting to strengthen collaboration. India pledged $500,000 to enhance the association’s institutional and financial capacities for effective cooperation.

items.title: Punjab University women's rafting team wins 2 golds, silver in grade 4 rapids
items.author: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK
items.description: Five brave women from Punjab took on the thrilling challenges of white-water rafting, kicking off their adventure with training sessions on a canal in Amritsar. At the 18th National Rafting Championship held in Uttarakhand, they astounded spectators by earning two gold medals, two silver medals, and an overall silver trophy in the women's category. This extraordinary feat underscores the rising prominence of women in Punjab's adventure sports landscape.

items.title: 14-year-old Iranian girl beaten to death by husband 10 days after giving birth
items.author: TOI WORLD DESK
items.description: A 14-year-old girl in Iran was allegedly killed by her husband just 10 days after giving birth, after asking to visit her family. Another pregnant woman was murdered by her husband the same day. The cases have renewed concerns over child marriage, domestic violence and femicide, with campaigners calling attention to gaps in legal protection.

items.title: Texas rock shelter yields 6,500-year-old kit with boomerang, darts and hide
items.author: WORLD DESK
items.description: In a remarkable archaeological find in West Texas, researchers uncovered a hunting kit that dates back approximately 6,000 years. The collection features various stone and wooden foreshafts, along with essential hunting tools, including a partial atlatl, which is an ancient spear-throwing apparatus. The diversity of materials suggests varying time periods, unlocking valuable insights into the lifestyles and surroundings of these ancient communities.

items.title: Indian citizenship: New citizens to get digital certificates; hard copy on request
items.author: BHARTI JAIN
items.description: Individuals acquiring Indian citizenship will receive a digital certificate instead of a physical copy. This change applies to those registered or naturalised as citizens. Applicants can request a hard copy if desired, as per the new amendments. The digital certificates will be signed by an authorized officer from the central government. These amendments aim to modernize the process of issuing citizenship certificates in India.

items.title: SC junks plea to remove Italian politician’s ‘vote chor’ remark on social media
items.author: TNN
items.description: The Supreme Court of India dismissed a plea concerning Giacomo Filibeck's remarks made during the Bharat Summit. Filibeck's slogan and comments on Rahul Gandhi sparked controversy within political spaces. Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh emphasized the right to file complaints.

items.title: Eagle talon marks on 3 baboon skulls raise questions about early human predators
items.author: TOI SCIENCE DESK
items.description: In a groundbreaking study, researchers in Chad have uncovered puncture marks on baboon skulls, suggesting that eagles may prey on these large primates. Out of five examined skulls, three displayed signs typical of eagle talon strikes. This startling discovery raises questions about baboons' vulnerability to aerial predators and encourages a reassessment of early hominin interactions with such threats, potentially reshaping our understanding of primate evolution.
